Subject: Marketplace add-on packaging & channel commission — private offer request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement here — we are close to approving the private offer but need clarity on two items before we move to signature:

1) Add-on packaging: We purchase the base inference SKU + two optional add-ons (LongContext and DedicatedKV). Can these be bundled into a single private-offer SKU with volume thresholds, or do they need distinct SKUs? If a bundle, what is the recommended pricing cadence (flat monthly vs. usage tiers)?

2) Channel commission / reseller pass-through: We work with PartnerCloud (cc'd). PartnerCloud expects a 12% commission on total net spend for introducing vendors. Is that compatible with Redwood's private-offer flows on AWS Marketplace? If not, what are the alternative routing/crediting options?

Attached are a short usage sample and our request doc. Please advise timelines — we'd like to close the PO by 11/30.

Best,

Acme Corp

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Marketplace add-on packaging & channel commission — private offer request

Maya — thanks for the note and the attachments. Quick answers up front, followed by details:

- Bundle vs separate SKUs: We can create a bundled private-offer SKU that includes Base + LongContext + DedicatedKV. For predictable finance and marketplace mapping we recommend a tiered volume model (monthly committed units with overage pricing) rather than a pure flat monthly, because your usage sample shows spikes.

- Channel commission: 12% is higher than our standard pass-through in AWS private-offer flows, but we can support equivalent economics via one of two patterns:
  * Route A (Marketplace pass-through): Redwood lists the private offer in your AWS account and the partner is paid through a reseller pass-through mechanism (works for most partners). This requires a 3-party agreement and will show on the invoice as a partner fee line item.
  * Route B (Credit-backed): Redwood provides a list-price concession at offer creation and issues a monthly rebate/credit to Acme; PartnerCloud invoices Acme separately for their 12% commission. This keeps the marketplace settlement simpler but requires a commercial crediting schedule to reconcile monthly.

I'll summarize tradeoffs below and propose a short call to pick the approach and get an updated PO by 11/30.

Tradeoffs:
- Route A keeps partner fees on the AWS settlement but requires partner onboarding on our Marketplace listing and increases billing complexity for Acme's AWS finance team.
- Route B simplifies AWS settlements but requires Acme to accept a rebate flow and a short reconciliation window (30 days).

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min call Tues 11/23 to lock packaging and commission path (I can include Ben — partner ops — and Laura — finance).
2) If Route A chosen: Ben will send partner onboarding checklist; if Route B: Laura will draft a monthly rebate cadence doc and sample invoice lines.

Can you confirm availability for 11/23 between 10–12 PT?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Principal Sales Manager, Cloud Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks, 11/23 10:30 PT works for me. A few clarifying points ahead of the call so we can prep:

- Commission mechanics: PartnerCloud is insisting the 12% be applied to net spend after marketplace fees (so their fee equals 12% of what we actually pay). If Route B is used, PartnerCloud wants a short statement of work that guarantees monthly remittance timing (within 15 days of month-end).

- Compliance: Can you confirm that using a bundle SKU affects our ability to retain audit logs (we need 7-year retention). That is a hard requirement.

Look forward to the call.
